key_insight: PhenSPINE introduces a standardized MRI benchmark and shows that adding positional context to deep models improves spine pathology diagnosis, with Sagittal T2-weighted images performing best.
clinical_relevance: The study suggests that careful MRI sequence selection and anatomy-aware modeling may improve automated support for spine pathology interpretation.
method: Built PhenSPINE from 16,813 MRI images across 250 patients.
Benchmarked deep learning models using state-of-the-art convolutional backbones plus positional encoding for disc-level context.
Compared four MRI sequences and multisequence fusion strategies for diagnosis.
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated MRI sequences, Sagittal T2-weighted imaging achieved the strongest result, with a Macro F1-score of 50.31%, and outperformed multisequence fusion in this dataset.
watch_item: Performance was limited by noise and interference from surrounding anatomy, so results may not generalize well without cleaner data or sequence-specific preprocessing.
paper_title: PhenSPINE: A Standardized Benchmark for Spine Pathology Diagnosis
